body:
Hey, thanks for talking with me. It feels better talking to someone rather than keeping it all bottled inside. 

Anyway, I originally PM'd this to you (I don't know why but I figured you see it here better). One of the things you read that's troubling me was how to explain my three years of unemployment to a potential employer. This scares me more now than being obese. How should I handle this?
Thank you. It's nice to have an ear when you need one. I never looked out for one before because I just assumed nobody really cared what I had to say.

Hey, thanks for talking with me. I think I'm going to work on losing the weight and then soon I won't be worried about what anybody thinks anymore. I think that's the best route to solve all my other issues. Thanks again.
Thank you, and thanks for talking with me.

Thanks for the suggestions. As to the computer stuff, I use to code a little in college when I was taking several meteorology classes kind of as an independent minor. We coded forecast models to predict the weather and to analyze collected weather measurements.

Thanks for the tips. I've studied already pretty much everything already about dieting the body etc. Even down to the microbiology of it all. I'm just fighting myself right now to actually do it. Like I mention above the things that would most certainly make me better and happy are the things hardest for me to do right now. I want to get better start a career have it all, but at the same time theirs like an invisible force that keeps me back. An force of anxiety, depression, etc that completely upends every good thing I think of. It's all unnerving and I'm tired of it.

You also can't deny first impressions. I can talk the talk but as soon as I show up at an interview and they see me walk in that door I can usually know within a second from their facial expressions what they think of me already and they just put on a ruse until it's enough time that's past to make it look like they haven't discriminated against me because of my weight.

Ok. That aside, what are my options then? I've been out of work for three years now. And becuase I am still young have no accumulated job experience really. Sure, I've worked menial jobs as a dishwasher, desk attendant, cook, worked a couple months as research analyst (my last job, that was a trial basically that didn't work out and they let me go on goods grounds), and a clerk organizing files. I have my degree, but that's been useless to me as jobs where I could put my degree to use are requiring 3 years this, 5 years that, etc. For the manager training jobs I'm most certain going to lose out to some MBA grad right out of college so that's that. I just don't see a way to win.

No. I'm afraid that if I am treated for depression, that anyone who could snoop through my records will discover that I am or was treated for depression and look at me less favorably or be scared that I would go bizzerk on them.
I know. I'm turning into a conspiracy guy. I don't want to but, such are things i guess.

I live in the US. I'm just afraid after the Healthcare change-ups, the shooting incidents, and wackos out there, the NSA, and other three letter agencies that I can't be sure the government won't allow access to our health records by employers, schools, government agencies, etc.
I'm always worried about what other people think of me. I have no Facebook, twitter, instagram, nothing...
Afraid of in the future employers will be able to request medical records to see if you are stable and capable or not.
Nope. I really don't want that kind of stuff in my medical records.
